newsitem.title: USA: Payless ShoeSource to buy back stock.
newsitem.headline: Payless ShoeSource to buy back stock.

text.p: Payless ShoeSource Inc said Tuesday its board of directors authorized the repurchase of up to $150 million worth of outstanding common stock in open market transactions.
The stock buy-back is subject to receipt of a favorable tax ruling from the Internal Revenue Service and market conditions, it added.

Payless, a footwear retailer with 4,261 stores, said the planned $150 million repurchase would represent about 4.3 million shares, or approximately 11 percent of its 39.9 million common shares outstanding.
The purchased shares will be held in the treasury for general corporate purposes.

Payless said it is seeking an IRS ruling to ensure that the stock repurchase complies with regulations applicable to companies that have been spun-off in tax-free distributions. Payless was spun off from May Department Stores Co in May 1996.
Payless said it expects to file the ruling request with the IRS promptly and hopes to receive a ruling within 120 days.

"The stock repurchase is an attractive investment and a good use of the company's cash," Steven Douglass, chairman, said in a statement. "We currently project that our cash flow is adequate to fund this repurchase, while continuing to support our core business and pursuing other strategic growth options...."
